hostSafeguards.name: clock
hostSafeguards.notes: Checks clock against remote HTTP time sources; syncs via hwclock/ntpdate/timedatectl if >5 minutes off
hostSafeguards.reason: Verify system clock accuracy for TLS certificate validation and JWT operations

hostSafeguards.name: dns_resolution
hostSafeguards.notes: Writes /etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/99-vrooli-dns.conf with Google and Cloudflare DNS; flushes cache
hostSafeguards.reason: Configure reliable DNS servers via systemd-resolved for resilient name resolution

hostSafeguards.name: docker_host_firewall
hostSafeguards.notes: Creates and wires VROOLI-DOCKER iptables chain into DOCKER-USER for container-to-host networking
hostSafeguards.reason: Enable Docker containers to reach native host services via iptables VROOLI-DOCKER chain

hostSafeguards.name: kernel_config
hostSafeguards.notes: Manages /etc/sysctl.d/99-vrooli.conf with inotify and other kernel parameters
hostSafeguards.reason: Configure kernel parameters for optimal Vrooli operation (inotify limits for dev servers)

hostSafeguards.name: workspace_sandbox_userns
hostSafeguards.notes: Installs/loads a dedicated vrooli-workspace-sandbox AppArmor profile when plain unshare is blocked; does not disable AppArmor or kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns globally.
hostSafeguards.reason: Allow workspace-sandbox to restart through its portable launcher with the default overlayfs-userns driver after Linux host reboots

hostSafeguards.name: nat_protection
hostSafeguards.notes: Scans iptables -t nat OUTPUT for REDIRECT rules whose target ports have no listener and removes them
hostSafeguards.reason: Detect and remove dead NAT iptables REDIRECT rules that hijack web traffic

hostSafeguards.name: remote_session_protection
hostSafeguards.notes: Native runtime applies managed Linux sysctl and systemd protections for remote sessions
hostSafeguards.reason: Protect remote Linux GUI sessions when the deployment profile calls for it

hostSafeguards.name: remote_desktop_access
hostSafeguards.notes: Declares remote desktop experience and reports provider support without overriding display-manager policy; remote-desktop credentials are held by Vrooli's encrypted credential authority, not the login keyring
hostSafeguards.reason: Make remote desktop behavior explicit and safe to inspect before applying

hostSafeguards.name: login_keyring_unlock
hostSafeguards.notes: High-risk, opt-in safeguard. On an autologin host, backs up the login keyring and opens the user's keyring prompt to request a blank passphrase. Any process running as the autologin user can then read secrets stored in the keyring.
hostSafeguards.reason: Make the login keyring available to an autologin session when the operator explicitly accepts the loss of encryption at rest

hostSafeguards.name: tcp_tuning
hostSafeguards.notes: Manages /etc/sysctl.d/99-vrooli-tcp.conf with tcp_ecn, tcp_mtu_probing, tcp_base_mss
hostSafeguards.reason: Optimize TCP stack for reliable connectivity (disable ECN, enable PMTU probing)

hostSafeguards.name: ollama_resource_controls
hostSafeguards.notes: Writes /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/99-vrooli-resource-controls.conf. Auto-skips on hosts without ollama.service. Operator must `systemctl restart ollama` to apply limits to the running process.
hostSafeguards.reason: Cap ollama.service memory and bias OOM killer toward it so an embeddings burst cannot exhaust host RAM (see 2026-05-07 host-stability investigation)

hostSafeguards.name: nvidia_driver
hostSafeguards.reason: Accelerator readiness is a host requirement, not a per-resource probe. The safeguard proves the NVIDIA driver is ready, that the compute device nodes survive a boot with no client attached, and that the invoking user can open them. Registering it here is what makes it run outside setup: without a develop-time registration the host is only checked at install, which is exactly when the device nodes are least likely to exist.
hostSafeguards.notes: No-op on hosts without NVIDIA display hardware. Optional because a CPU fallback is a supported, reported state; a resource that must have an accelerator declares acceleration.require = required.

hostSafeguards.name: host_hardening
hostSafeguards.notes: Writes /etc/sysctl.d/99-vrooli-host-hardening.conf and /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/99-vrooli-ratelimit.conf. Depends on the kdump-tools tool being armed (Phase 2 of 2026-05-07 work) — without that, panic_on_oops=1 turns survivable oopses into reboots that produce no diagnostics.
hostSafeguards.reason: Turn silent hard resets into observable kdump-able panics (sysrq, hung_task/softlockup/NMI/oops panic) and rate-limit journald so UFW BLOCK floods don't drown panic info

hostSafeguards.name: vrooli_launcher
hostSafeguards.notes: Optional: only matters if you want `sudo vrooli ...` to work. The shim forwards to the calling user's ~/.vrooli/bin/vrooli; see internal/safeguards/vrooli-launcher/handler.go package doc for the design rationale.
hostSafeguards.reason: Install /usr/local/bin/vrooli launcher shim so `sudo vrooli` resolves (sudo's secure_path excludes ~/.vrooli/bin where make install writes the real binary)

hostSafeguards.name: pstore_native
hostSafeguards.notes: Loads efi_pstore (UEFI hosts) and/or erst (ACPI ERST hosts) and persists at-boot via /etc/modules-load.d. Reports SupportNotApplicable when neither backend is available; configure pstore_ramoops as a RAM-backed fallback in that case.
hostSafeguards.reason: Activate native kernel pstore backends (efi_pstore / erst) so panic dumps survive resets without modifying GRUB

hostSafeguards.name: pstore_observability
hostSafeguards.notes: Creates the vrooli-observability group, adds the invoking project user, installs a root-owned pstore collector service/timer, and exports artifacts read-only. Does not delete /sys/fs/pstore artifacts. A logout/login or reboot may be needed before the current shell observes new group membership.
hostSafeguards.reason: Export root-readable pstore crash artifacts into /var/lib/vrooli/host-observability/pstore so unprivileged scenarios can inspect crash evidence without sudo

hostSafeguards.name: kdump_observability
hostSafeguards.notes: Installs a root-owned collector service/timer that exports a bounded panic summary from each /var/crash dump into /var/lib/vrooli/host-observability/crashdumps. The vmcore itself is never copied. Retention prunes only kdump's own timestamp directories, only beyond the newest retain_vmcores, and only once that dump's summary exists; anything else in /var/crash is left alone. Requires the same vrooli-observability group as pstore_observability, so a logout/login may be needed before the current shell sees membership.
hostSafeguards.reason: Make kernel panics visible to unprivileged scenarios: kdump writes a complete record to /var/crash but the dmesg is mode 0600 root and the vmcore is roughly the size of RAM, so on 2026-08-19 a host panic left perfect evidence that nothing in Vrooli could read

hostSafeguards.name: pstore_ramoops
hostSafeguards.notes: Modifies GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub. Backup written to /etc/default/grub.vrooli-bak.<timestamp>. REQUIRES OPERATOR REBOOT — Vrooli does NOT auto-run update-grub. Configure mem_address and mem_size in operator-state when native pstore is unavailable.
hostSafeguards.reason: RAM-backed pstore fallback for hosts without native pstore — opt-in only, requires explicit memory-region configuration

hostSafeguards.name: crashkernel_reserve
hostSafeguards.notes: Modifies GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX with crashkernel=512M-:256M (overridable via the reservation parameter). Backup written. REQUIRES OPERATOR REBOOT after running `sudo update-grub`.
hostSafeguards.reason: Reserve memory for the kdump capture kernel via the crashkernel= boot parameter so kdump-tools can capture panics

hostSafeguards.name: netconsole
hostSafeguards.notes: Loads the netconsole kernel module with the operator-supplied target parameter (kernel netconsole format: src-port@src-ip/dev,tgt-port@tgt-ip/tgt-mac). Reports an invalid parameter when unset.
hostSafeguards.reason: Stream kernel oops/panic output to a remote log collector for off-host crash forensics

hostSafeguards.name: edac_modules
hostSafeguards.notes: Detects CPU vendor/family and modprobes the matching EDAC driver (currently amd64_edac for AMD Family 15h–1Ah). Reports SupportNotApplicable on consumer Ryzen 7000 where ECC is not exposed by firmware.
hostSafeguards.reason: Load EDAC drivers so memory error counters become readable under /sys/devices/system/edac/ on supported chipsets

hostSafeguards.name: tpm_credential_access
hostSafeguards.notes: Adds the invoking operator account to the group owning /dev/tpmrm0 (usually tss). Auto-skips on hosts with no TPM, or where the device grants its group nothing. Setup picks the grant up in its own credential stage and adds the unattended wrap in the same run; no logout and no second command.
hostSafeguards.reason: Let the encrypted credential store open itself from the TPM after a reboot, instead of requiring an operator to type a passphrase at every boot

hostSafeguards.name: autoheal_watchdog
hostSafeguards.notes: Installs and verifies the autoheal loop in the invoking user's native scheduler. Dedicated-host policy enables Linux lingering for pre-login startup; shared-host policy remains login-scoped.
hostSafeguards.reason: Ensure the supervisor that repairs failed workloads survives reboot and is not dependent on a separate scenario install command

hostSafeguards.name: emergency_watchdog
hostSafeguards.notes: Installs ~/.vrooli/libexec/emergency-watchdog.sh plus a systemd user service and timer under the invoking user's home. Needs no privilege. Replaces scripts/emergency-watchdog.sh, which was referenced by runbooks, installed by nothing, and whose hand-created unit hard-coded one operator's repository path. Holds unit restarts while CPU PSI shows the host is saturated.
hostSafeguards.reason: Give setup ownership of the last line of defense so every host has it, rather than depending on a hand-placed systemd unit that existed on exactly one machine

hostSafeguards.name: coding_agent_shims
hostSafeguards.notes: Installs alias links (codex, claude, grok, opencode, agy) in ~/.vrooli/bin pointing at vrooli-agent-launcher, which attributes the run and then execs the real agent. Needs no privilege. Replaces the bash functions sourced from ~/.bashrc, which covered only interactive bash on Linux, had no installer, and could not be upgraded or removed.
hostSafeguards.reason: Attribute coding-agent runs started from any shell, including non-interactive ones, instead of only from an interactive bash that happened to source a profile snippet

hostTools.name: git
hostTools.rationale: The control plane needs Git to identify and operate on the source tree during setup and development.
hostTools.reason: Support repository bootstrap, source operations, and setup-time git configuration

hostTools.name: curl
hostTools.rationale: Setup and lifecycle helpers retrieve release metadata and artifacts over HTTP.
hostTools.reason: Support HTTP-based bootstrap, diagnostics, and resource helper flows

hostTools.name: jq
hostTools.rationale: The documented operator and validation workflows require a portable JSON command-line parser.
hostTools.reason: Support JSON parsing. Commonly used by coding agents and scripts

hostTools.name: yq
hostTools.rationale: The documented operator and validation workflows require a portable YAML command-line parser.
hostTools.reason: Support YAML parsing. Commonly used by coding agents and scripts

hostTools.name: docker
hostTools.reason: Run containerized resources across setup modes

hostTools.name: go
hostTools.rationale: The Go toolchain is required to build and validate the control plane itself.
hostTools.reason: Build and validate native Vrooli tooling during development setup

hostTools.name: node
hostTools.reason: Build and run JavaScript-based workspace tooling during development setup

hostTools.name: pnpm
hostTools.notes: Pinned standalone binary matching the pnpm-workspace.yaml packageManager version; installed into ~/.vrooli/bin (no sudo).
hostTools.reason: Install and build scenario UI workspaces; lifecycle steps fall back to plain `pnpm` when the host Node.js has no corepack shims

hostTools.name: python
hostTools.reason: Support repo validation helpers and Python-based flows during development setup

hostTools.name: java
hostTools.reason: Provide Java 17+ for formal verification backends used by Quint verify

hostTools.name: quint
hostTools.notes: Pinned to 0.32.0; installed via internal/tools/quint Go handler from @informalsystems/quint.
hostTools.reason: Check formal temporal-flow models and generate deterministic model-based test artifacts

hostTools.name: buf
hostTools.notes: Pinned to v1.37.0; installed via internal/tools/buf Go handler (no shell installer). See docs/development/proto.md.
hostTools.reason: Drive packages/proto codegen, lint, and breaking-change checks; also gates template validation

hostTools.name: protoc-gen-go
hostTools.notes: Pinned alongside packages/proto/buf.gen.yaml; installed via `go install`.
hostTools.reason: Local protoc plugin for Go codegen; replaces the BSR remote plugin so packages/proto generates offline

hostTools.name: protoc-gen-connect-go
hostTools.notes: Pinned alongside packages/proto/buf.gen.yaml; installed via `go install`.
hostTools.reason: Local Connect-RPC protoc plugin for Go service codegen; keeps packages/proto generation offline

hostTools.name: protoc-gen-es
hostTools.notes: Pinned alongside packages/proto/buf.gen.yaml; installed via npm into ~/.cache/vrooli/protoc-plugins/node.
hostTools.reason: Local protoc plugin for TypeScript/JavaScript codegen; replaces the BSR remote plugin

hostTools.name: protoc
hostTools.notes: v25+ required for both --python_out and --pyi_out built-ins.
hostTools.reason: Provides built-in Python and pyi codegen invoked by buf via protoc_builtin; replaces the BSR remote python/pyi plugins

hostTools.name: rasdaemon
hostTools.notes: Custom handler enables and starts rasdaemon.service; events recorded to /var/lib/rasdaemon/ras-mc_event.db for ras-mc-ctl.
hostTools.reason: Capture AMD/Intel hardware error events (MCE, EDAC, PCIe AER) so unexplained host resets can be diagnosed via the system-mce-recent autoheal check

hostTools.name: mcelog
hostTools.notes: Custom handler enables mcelog.service; on modern AMD systems mcelog is often masked because rasdaemon owns the MCE channel — that is treated as ExecutionAlreadyPresent, not a failure.
hostTools.reason: Capture Machine Check Exceptions on hosts where rasdaemon is unavailable; otherwise treated as superseded

hostTools.name: kdump-tools
hostTools.notes: Custom handler preseeds debconf and installs noninteractively. Reports ExecutionRebootRequired until crashkernel= appears in /proc/cmdline (provided by the crashkernel_reserve safeguard).
hostTools.reason: Capture full kernel crash dumps on panic to /var/crash for forensic analysis of unexplained resets
